start.title: Getting started: sign-up, verification, activation
start.intro: An ADA Pro space opens only after the AccesDirectAide team has verified the organisation against an official source.
start.s1.title: Ask for the space to be opened
start.s1.body: Enter the organisation's name, its SIRET number (14 digits), your work e-mail and a password, then accept the terms of use. If the page says that sign-up is not open, partner organisations are created by the AccesDirectAide team and their members receive a personal invitation.
start.s2.title: Wait for the verification
start.s2.body: The AccesDirectAide team verifies the organisation against an official source. Until then your space is not open: the sign-in says that your request has been received. The app gives no delay; you receive an e-mail as soon as the verification is done.
start.s3.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
start.s3.body: The opening e-mail contains a link to turn on two-factor authentication. Open it while signed in, add the secret to an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy or FreeOTP), then enter the 6-digit code. The password alone is not enough: where it is required, an account without two-factor authentication can only open this page.
start.s4.title: Sign in every day
start.s4.body: Enter your professional login and your password, then the code shown by your app. If your address belongs to several organisations, the page asks you to choose the one to open.
start.s5.title: Join an organisation by invitation
start.s5.body: An administrator of the organisation invites you from “My team”. The link received by e-mail opens the “Join the team” page: you create your password and accept the terms of use.
structure.title: Set up the organisation's record
structure.intro: The public record is the one verified by ADA. A record not yet verified does not appear in the public directory.
structure.s1.title: Review the public record
structure.s1.body: “My organisation” shows the record as verified by ADA, with the verification date. The dashboard also shows whether the record is active, suspended or awaiting activation.
structure.s2.title: Propose a change
structure.s2.body: Choose the information to change, enter the new value and send the proposal. Nothing is published directly: the ADA team checks every proposal before publication. While it is pending, you can withdraw it.
structure.s3.title: Export the data or close the space
structure.s3.body: The bottom of the page lets you export the organisation's data and ask for the space to be closed. The closure is reviewed by the ADA team; first export the data you need.
services.title: Create services and choose the needs
services.intro: A service is a reason for an appointment: a name, a duration and the formats offered. Only administrators create or change services; the other members can view them.
services.s1.title: Create a service
services.s1.body: In “Appointment services”, choose “New service”: name, duration in minutes, buffer time before and after, “Service active”, and at least one format (in person or remotely by video).
services.s2.title: Choose the needs it meets
services.s2.body: Choose up to {{max}} needs from AccesDirectAide's common list (20 domains, 86 sub-domains). They describe your service, never the person. With no need chosen, the place does not appear when someone looks for where to book an appointment for a need.
services.s3.title: Offer video calls
services.s3.body: Video is offered to people only if the organisation accepts it (booking mode “Video” or “In person + video call”) and if the video service is turned on. The room opens from the page of each video appointment.
hours.title: Set the availability
hours.intro: The availability is the organisation's opening hours: the slots offered come from it.
hours.s1.title: Add time ranges
hours.s1.body: For each day, add one or more ranges (HH:MM-HH:MM) or leave the day closed, then save. For the other members the page is read-only.
hours.s2.title: Give the schedule to a member
hours.s2.body: In “My team”, the “Manages the schedule” option lets a professional change the team's hours and absences.
publish.title: Publish online appointment booking
publish.intro: Publishing makes your booking page visible to people. Only administrators can publish or unpublish.
publish.s1.title: Prepare before publishing
publish.s1.body: Create at least one active service and set the availability: without them no slot can be offered. The server only checks that appointments are installed; if they are not, the publish box is locked and the screen explains why.
publish.s2.title: Choose the confirmation rules
publish.s2.body: Direct confirmation (the slot is confirmed as soon as it is requested) or approval by the organisation (the request waits for your agreement), for the whole organisation or per service. You can also let people choose a professional; a member without two-factor authentication cannot receive online appointments, and a member without a public name is never shown.
publish.s3.title: Publish
publish.s3.body: Tick “Publish online appointment booking”, choose the booking mode (in person, video or both), add a contact e-mail and phone if needed, then “Save the settings”. The address of the public page is then shown. Publishing and withdrawing are recorded in the audit log.
publish.s4.title: You already have your own booking tool
publish.s4.body: Enter the https address of your booking page (your website or a public platform such as RDV Solidarités). After AccesDirectAide has checked it, your record shows a “Book on their website” link.
agenda.title: Every day: calendar and booking
agenda.intro: All active members use the calendar and create appointments for the people they see.
agenda.s1.title: Follow the calendar
agenda.s1.body: Filter by service, status and period. A pending request is handled with “Accept the request” or “Decline the request”; after the appointment, mark the person as present or absent. A cancellation informs the person. The calendar can be exported in .ics format.
agenda.s2.title: Create an appointment for someone
agenda.s2.body: Choose the service and a period, load the slots, select one, then enter the person's name (phone optional). Tick the box confirming their agreement to this appointment and to the recording of their contact details, then “Confirm the appointment”.
agenda.s3.title: Open an appointment
agenda.s3.body: The page of an appointment shows its details, any rescheduling and, if the person has an account, the related messages. For a video appointment, the room opens from this page.
absences.title: Absences and closures
absences.intro: A member's absence does not close the organisation; closing the whole organisation removes the slots offered to the public.
absences.s1.title: Declare your absence
absences.s1.body: Choose “Myself”, a start and an end date, and a reason if you wish. The reason is shown only to you and to the people who manage the schedule.
absences.s2.title: Close the whole organisation
absences.s2.body: Choose “The whole organisation”: no more online slots during the period. Only the administrator or a member who manages the schedule can close the organisation or change a colleague's absence.
messages.title: Secure messaging
messages.intro: Messages are encrypted at rest on our servers and every access is logged. This is not end-to-end encryption: our servers hold the keys.
messages.s1.title: Reply to people
messages.s1.body: Conversations appear when a person contacts you through appointment booking. The menu may show the number of unread conversations. A person without an account cannot receive messages.
messages.s2.title: Write only what is useful
messages.s2.body: No health information and no diagnosis: this messaging is not a case file. Attachments are not open yet, because a file may contain health information, which requires certified hosting.
team.title: Team and roles
team.intro: Two roles: Organisation administrator (record, team, services, publishing, impact, audit log) and Professional (calendar, appointments, messages, their own absences; services and availability read-only).
team.s1.title: Invite a colleague
team.s1.body: Enter their e-mail and role, then “Invite”. Pending invitations can be sent again or cancelled. If the e-mail could not be sent, the screen says so: send it again later.
team.s2.title: Give a public name
team.s2.body: The public name lets people choose a professional when the organisation allows it; the e-mail address is never shown. Everyone can also set it in “Settings”.
team.s3.title: Remove a colleague
team.s3.body: Choose “Deactivate”, then say who takes over their open files (a successor or the team queue) and confirm. The account can be reactivated later.
team.s4.title: Lost device
team.s4.body: First check the person's identity in a safe way, then “Lost device”: their authenticator stops working, their sessions end and a new invitation, valid for 72 hours, is sent to them.
privacy.title: Protect people's data
privacy.intro: The rules below repeat the instructions shown by the app.
privacy.s1.title: No health data in free-text fields
privacy.s1.body: The messaging forbids health information and diagnoses. As a precaution, apply the same rule to appointment notes and absence reasons: write only what is useful for the appointment.
privacy.s2.title: Collect the person's agreement
privacy.s2.body: An appointment created by the team asks you to confirm the person's agreement. For a service whose nature may reveal health information or a disability, their explicit agreement is required; some sensitive services are not open to booking on the platform.
privacy.s3.title: Secure your account
privacy.s3.body: Keep two-factor authentication on and sign out on a shared computer. Notification e-mails contain neither names nor file content; everything stays visible in the app.
audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: The log records the organisation's actions and accesses (sign-ins, invitations, files viewed, publishing…). It is reserved for administrators.
audit.s1.title: Read and export the log
audit.s1.body: Filter by action, browse the pages and export in CSV format. The IP address only appears in a shortened, transformed form. If loading fails, the screen states that it is not an empty log.
impact.title: Read the organisation's impact
impact.intro: Measured indicators, without estimates, reserved for administrators.
impact.s1.title: Choose the period
impact.s1.body: Month, quarter or year: appointments attended, conversations, recorded no-shows, active team, breakdown by service and by status. Small numbers are hidden. An SMS reminder “accepted by the operator” does not mean received. A function that is not open is marked “not measured”.
regional.title: Read the territorial observatory
regional.intro: Aggregates of verified organisations, without any access to named files. It is reserved for active organisations verified by ADA.
regional.s1.title: Understand the figures
regional.s1.body: A municipality is shown only from 3 organisations and values below 5 are hidden. The last quarter is published only once frozen.
settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Notifications, public name, password and two-factor authentication.
settings.s1.title: Set your notifications
settings.s1.body: All notifications stay visible in the app; you choose which ones are also sent to you by e-mail.
settings.s2.title: Change your password
settings.s2.body: The change is made through a link sent to your e-mail address (“Get the link”). No integration with an outside tool is available for now.
faq.q1: How long does the verification of the organisation take?
faq.a1: The app gives no delay. The verification is done by the AccesDirectAide team against an official source; you receive an e-mail as soon as it is finished.
faq.q2: The sign-in says my request has been received. Why?
faq.a2: Your organisation is not verified yet: the space opens only after the verification. Wait for the opening e-mail.
faq.a3: The public record verified by ADA and, if you published it, the booking page with your services and the available slots. A professional is shown only by their public name, if the organisation lets people choose; their e-mail address is never shown.
faq.q4: Is an account needed to book an appointment?
faq.a4: Yes. People must have a personal account to ask for an appointment; booking without an account no longer exists.
faq.q5: How do I unpublish appointment booking?
faq.a5: In “Appointment services”, untick “Publish online appointment booking”, then “Save the settings”. The withdrawal is recorded in the audit log. For a temporary closure, you can also close the whole organisation in “Absences”.
faq.q6: How do I remove a colleague who leaves the organisation?
faq.a6: An administrator opens “My team”, chooses “Deactivate”, says who takes over their open files (a successor or the team queue) and confirms.
faq.q7: I lost my two-factor authentication phone.
faq.a7: Ask an administrator of your organisation to use “Lost device” in “My team”, after checking your identity. You receive a new invitation valid for 72 hours. If nobody else administers the organisation, contact AccesDirectAide support.
faq.q8: Why can't I turn on two-factor authentication by myself?
faq.a8: To protect your account, it can only be turned on with an invitation sent by an administrator of your organisation. Open the link received by e-mail while signed in.
faq.a9: On the sign-in page, choose “Forgotten?”: you receive a reset link by e-mail.
faq.q10: Why does a member not receive online appointments?
faq.a10: A member whose two-factor authentication is not turned on cannot receive online appointments. If choosing a professional is turned on, also check that “Receives appointments” is ticked for them in the booking rules.
faq.q11: Why does my place not appear for a need?
faq.a11: The service must have needs chosen, and the organisation must be verified by ADA. With no need chosen, the place does not appear when someone looks for where to book an appointment for that need.
faq.q12: Can a professional change the opening hours?
faq.a12: Only if an administrator has given them the schedule (“Manages the schedule”). Otherwise the availability is read-only; everyone can declare their own absences.
faq.q13: How do I correct the address or the opening hours of the public record?
faq.a13: An administrator sends a proposal from “My organisation”. It is published after the ADA team has checked it.
faq.a14: No. They are encrypted at rest on our servers, which hold the keys, and every access is logged.
faq.a15: Not yet: a file may contain health information, which requires certified hosting. Write your message without a document.
faq.q16: Why are “Followed files” or “Referrals” marked “not open yet”?
faq.a16: These modules will open once their data-protection framework (and certified hosting for health data) is in place. It is not an outage.
faq.q17: Who sees the audit log and the impact?
faq.a17: Only the organisation's administrators. These entries do not appear in a professional's menu.
faq.a18: So that nobody can be recognised: the impact hides small numbers and the observatory hides values below 5.
faq.q19: Can the calendar be linked to Outlook?
faq.a19: The dashboard offers “Connect Outlook” when this link is turned on at ADA; otherwise it shows “Outlook (not turned on yet)”. The calendar can also be exported in .ics format.
faq.q20: How do I close the organisation's space?
faq.a20: An administrator chooses “Ask for closing” in “My organisation”. The ADA team reviews the request; first export the data you need.
faq.q21: My session ended for no apparent reason.
faq.a21: A session ends after a sign-out, a new password, a change in your team or when its time has run out. Sign in again: the page you asked for then opens.
faq.a22: Use the “Contact support” link on the sign-in page, or the link below.
trouble.pending: Wait for the opening e-mail: the verification is not done yet.
trouble.too_many: Wait a few minutes before trying again; check the login and the password.
trouble.bad_code: Enter the current code (it changes every 30 seconds) and check that your phone's time is correct.
trouble.disabled: Only an administrator of the organisation can reactivate the account from “My team”.
trouble.invitation_invalid: An administrator can send the invitation again from “My team”.
trouble.not_installed: This is not your mistake: tell the ADA team.
trouble.no_slots: Widen the period, then check the availability, the absences and whether the organisation is closed.
trouble.sensitive: Record this appointment in your usual tool, as the screen says.
trouble.too_many_requests: Wait a moment, then try again once.
trouble.queue_inactive: Your organisation has not been activated by ADA yet: check its status in “My organisation”.
trouble.regional: The observatory will open after your organisation has been activated.
trouble.audit: Try again; if the problem continues, contact support.

title: ADA Pro guide
intro: How AccesDirectAide's professional space works for social and medico-social organisations: from the opening request to everyday appointments.
public.note: This guide can be read without an account. The steps marked “after activation” are done once your organisation's space has been verified and opened.
public.register: Ask for the space to be opened
role_admin: You are an administrator of the organisation: all the steps concern you.
role_pro: The steps marked “Administrators” are done by an administrator of your organisation.
closed.intro: In the public beta these modules cannot be used: the menu lists them under “Not open yet”, without a link. The guide therefore does not describe how they work.
